# Selective MLP precision: prospective experiment

Whole-backbone BF16 and FP16 casts previously failed the unchanged numerical
gates (`benchmarks/real/mlx-bf16-screen77.json` and
`benchmarks/real/mlx-fp16-screen77.json`). This separate hypothesis changes only
selected MLP projection products. It introduces no production dtype policy.

The fixed family is all 28 down projections, all 28 gate/up projections, all
28 complete MLPs, first four complete MLPs, last four complete MLPs, and the last
complete MLP. The last-layer arm is diagnostic only. Its small conditional
uniform-layer ceiling is a budget decision, not a proof that a gain is impossible.
No failed arm will be replaced with an adaptively smaller arm.

First, every selected checkpoint parameter must be finite and survive exact
BF16 → FP32 → FP16 → FP32 value equality. BF16 significand width alone does not
establish this: FP16 has a narrower exponent range and a different subnormal
grid. Missing, malformed, overlapping or out-of-bounds selected tensor spans
are errors. Finite but inexact weights make the corresponding arms ineligible;
the guard will not be relaxed after observing them. Each arm is derived from
exactly its selected tensors, so failures in unselected embedding or attention
weights cannot reject an MLP arm.

`benchmarks.analysis.mlx.eligibility` reads the 84 BF16 MLP tensors in bounded
262,144-element CPU chunks using NumPy. It imports neither Torch nor MLX and
does not allocate a model. The validated artifact identity, before/after
checkpoint SHA256, source archive, per-tensor counts, finite-error maxima,
overflow, underflow-to-zero and BF16-source-subnormal counts are retained.
An overflow has infinite absolute error; the reported *finite* maximum is
therefore not an overall error bound when overflow is present. Partial receipts
are written after each tensor. The parent kills its owned child after 120 seconds
and preserves timeout/error status. Existing receipt names are never overwritten.
A completed scan with no eligible arm returns exit 1 and is a valid negative
eligibility result, distinct from an incomplete error or timeout.

Prepared command, requiring the coordinator's compute release before execution:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m benchmarks.analysis.mlx.eligibility \
  --model .models/Decision-2.0-Kai-0.6B \
  --output benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-mlp-fp16-eligibility.json
```

If any wider arm is eligible, a separately reviewed experiment will round only
the selected projection inputs to FP16, call maintained matmul/Linear with exact
FP16-stored weights, and restore each product to FP32 before maintained SwiGLU
or residual addition. Embeddings, attention, norms, residuals and head remain
FP32. This still approximates activations and output values: float accumulation
does not undo input or final FP16 output rounding. Ordinary FP32 × FP16 matmul
promotes its operands, so merely reducing stored weight dtype is not this test.
See the maintained-source audit in [storage.md](storage.md).

The eager full-prefill FP32 baseline stays unchanged. Candidate backbones share
immutable unmodified arrays and own replaced MLP modules. No prefix resource
built under one arithmetic policy may be reused under another. The worker must
set `MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0` before framework import. Both scalar and batch-eight
screens use the frozen 77-case CPU reference, original candidate order, recipe
and strict gates: logit atol/rtol 0.001, probability atol 0.0001, exact full ranks
and top choice, no accuracy loss, finite values and complete coverage.

Only eligible wider arms that pass both screens may receive five warmed,
alternating whole-cohort timing pairs, in the declared family order. Every warm
and measured cycle must independently pass the CPU reference gates. Promotion
requires median paired speedup ≥1.02 and paired sample p05 >1 at both shapes.
Repeated timing on this same cohort is performance confirmation, not independent
quality validation. Before any production proposal, varied menus and longer
admitted native DMBench cases must also challenge unchanged numerical behavior.
If all weights are ineligible, inference and timing will not run; any subsequent
BF16-native activation or custom accumulator hypothesis needs a fresh declaration.

"""
NumPy
=====

Provides
  1. An array object of arbitrary homogeneous items
  2. Fast mathematical operations over arrays
  3. Linear Algebra, Fourier Transforms, Random Number Generation

How to use the documentation
----------------------------
Documentation is available in two forms: docstrings provided
with the code, and a loose standing reference guide, available from
`the NumPy homepage <https://numpy.org>`_.

We recommend exploring the docstrings using
`IPython <https://ipython.org>`_, an advanced Python shell with
TAB-completion and introspection capabilities.  See below for further
instructions.

The docstring examples assume that `numpy` has been imported as ``np``::

  >>> import numpy as np

Code snippets are indicated by three greater-than signs::

  >>> x = 42
  >>> x = x + 1

Use the built-in ``help`` function to view a function's docstring::

  >>> help(np.sort)
  ... # doctest: +SKIP

For some objects, ``np.info(obj)`` may provide additional help.  This is
particularly true if you see the line "Help on ufunc object:" at the top
of the help() page.  Ufuncs are implemented in C, not Python, for speed.
The native Python help() does not know how to view their help, but our
np.info() function does.

Available subpackages
---------------------
lib
    Basic functions used by several sub-packages.
random
    Core Random Tools
linalg
    Core Linear Algebra Tools
fft
    Core FFT routines
polynomial
    Polynomial tools
testing
    NumPy testing tools

Utilities
---------
test
    Run numpy unittests
show_config
    Show numpy build configuration
__version__
    NumPy version string

Viewing documentation using IPython
-----------------------------------

Start IPython and import `numpy` usually under the alias ``np``: `import
numpy as np`.  Then, directly past or use the ``%cpaste`` magic to paste
examples into the shell.  To see which functions are available in `numpy`,
type ``np.<TAB>`` (where ``<TAB>`` refers to the TAB key), or use
``np.*cos*?<ENTER>`` (where ``<ENTER>`` refers to the ENTER key) to narrow
down the list.  To view the docstring for a function, use
``np.cos?<ENTER>`` (to view the docstring) and ``np.cos??<ENTER>`` (to view
the source code).

Copies vs. in-place operation
-----------------------------
Most of the functions in `numpy` return a copy of the array argument
(e.g., `np.sort`).  In-place versions of these functions are often
available as array methods, i.e. ``x = np.array([1,2,3]); x.sort()``.
Exceptions to this rule are documented.

"""

    # public submodules are imported lazily, therefore are accessible from
    # __getattr__. Note that `array_api`
    # (experimental label) is not added here, because `from numpy import *`
    # must not raise any warnings - that's too disruptive.
    __numpy_submodules__ = {
        "linalg", "fft", "dtypes", "random", "polynomial", "ma",
        "exceptions", "lib", "ctypeslib", "testing", "typing",
        "f2py", "test", "rec", "char", "core", "strings",
    }

    # We build warning messages for former attributes
    _msg = (
        "module 'numpy' has no attribute '{n}'.\n"
        "`np.{n}` was a deprecated alias for the builtin `{n}`. "
        "To avoid this error in existing code, use `{n}` by itself. "
        "Doing this will not modify any behavior and is safe. {extended_msg}\n"
        "The aliases was originally deprecated in NumPy 1.20; for more "
        "details and guidance see the original release note at:\n"
        "    https://numpy.org/devdocs/release/1.20.0-notes.html#deprecations")

    _specific_msg = (
        "If you specifically wanted the numpy scalar type, use `np.{}` here.")

    _int_extended_msg = (
        "When replacing `np.{}`, you may wish to use e.g. `np.int64` "
        "or `np.int32` to specify the precision. If you wish to review "
        "your current use, check the release note link for "
        "additional information.")

    _type_info = [
        ("object", ""),  # The NumPy scalar only exists by name.
        ("float", _specific_msg.format("float64")),
        ("complex", _specific_msg.format("complex128")),
        ("str", _specific_msg.format("str_")),
        ("int", _int_extended_msg.format("int"))]

    __former_attrs__ = {
         n: _msg.format(n=n, extended_msg=extended_msg)
         for n, extended_msg in _type_info
     }

    # Some of these could be defined right away, but most were aliases to
    # the Python objects and only removed in NumPy 1.24.  Defining them should
    # probably wait for NumPy 1.26 or 2.0.
    # When defined, these should possibly not be added to `__all__` to avoid
    # import with `from numpy import *`.
    __future_scalars__ = {"str", "bytes", "object"}

    __array_api_version__ = "2025.12"

    from ._array_api_info import __array_namespace_info__

    __all__ = list(
        __numpy_submodules__ |
        set(_core.__all__) |
        set(_mat.__all__) |
        set(lib._histograms_impl.__all__) |
        set(lib._nanfunctions_impl.__all__) |
        set(lib._function_base_impl.__all__) |
        set(lib._twodim_base_impl.__all__) |
        set(lib._shape_base_impl.__all__) |
        set(lib._type_check_impl.__all__) |
        set(lib._arraysetops_impl.__all__) |
        set(lib._ufunclike_impl.__all__) |
        set(lib._arraypad_impl.__all__) |
        set(lib._utils_impl.__all__) |
        set(lib._stride_tricks_impl.__all__) |
        set(lib._polynomial_impl.__all__) |
        set(lib._npyio_impl.__all__) |
        set(lib._index_tricks_impl.__all__) |
        {"emath", "show_config", "__version__", "__array_namespace_info__"}
    )

    # Filter out Cython harmless warnings
    warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message="numpy.dtype size changed")
    warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message="numpy.ufunc size changed")
    warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message="numpy.ndarray size changed")

    def __getattr__(attr):
        # Warn for expired attributes
        import warnings

        if attr == "linalg":
            import numpy.linalg as linalg
            return linalg
        elif attr == "fft":
            import numpy.fft as fft
            return fft
        elif attr == "dtypes":
            import numpy.dtypes as dtypes
            return dtypes
        elif attr == "random":
            import numpy.random as random
            return random
        elif attr == "polynomial":
            import numpy.polynomial as polynomial
            return polynomial
        elif attr == "ma":
            import numpy.ma as ma
            return ma
        elif attr == "ctypeslib":
            import numpy.ctypeslib as ctypeslib
            return ctypeslib
        elif attr == "exceptions":
            import numpy.exceptions as exceptions
            return exceptions
        elif attr == "testing":
            import numpy.testing as testing
            return testing
        elif attr == "matlib":
            import numpy.matlib as matlib
            return matlib
        elif attr == "f2py":
            import numpy.f2py as f2py
            return f2py
        elif attr == "typing":
            import numpy.typing as typing
            return typing
        elif attr == "rec":
            import numpy.rec as rec
            return rec
        elif attr == "char":
            import numpy.char as char
            return char
        elif attr == "core":
            import numpy.core as core
            return core
        elif attr == "strings":
            import numpy.strings as strings
            return strings
        if attr in __future_scalars__:
            # And future warnings for those that will change, but also give
            # the AttributeError
            warnings.warn(
                f"In the future `np.{attr}` will be defined as the "
                "corresponding NumPy scalar.", FutureWarning, stacklevel=2)

        if attr in __former_attrs__:
            raise AttributeError(__former_attrs__[attr], name=None)

        if attr in __expired_attributes__:
            raise AttributeError(
                f"`np.{attr}` was removed in the NumPy 2.0 release. "
                f"{__expired_attributes__[attr]}",
                name=None
            )

        raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {attr!r}")

    def __dir__():
        public_symbols = (
            globals().keys() | __numpy_submodules__
        )
        public_symbols -= {
            "matrixlib", "matlib", "tests", "conftest", "version",
            "array_api"
        }
        return list(public_symbols)

    # Pytest testing
    from numpy._pytesttester import PytestTester
    test = PytestTester(__name__)
    del PytestTester

    def _sanity_check():
        """
        Quick sanity checks for common bugs caused by environment.
        There are some cases e.g. with wrong BLAS ABI that cause wrong
        results under specific runtime conditions that are not necessarily
        achieved during test suite runs, and it is useful to catch those early.

        See https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/8577 and other
        similar bug reports.

        """
        try:
            x = ones(2, dtype=float32)
            if not abs(x.dot(x) - float32(2.0)) < 1e-5:
                raise AssertionError
        except AssertionError:
            msg = ("The current Numpy installation ({!r}) fails to "
                   "pass simple sanity checks. This can be caused for example "
                   "by incorrect BLAS library being linked in, or by mixing "
                   "package managers (pip, conda, apt, ...). Search closed "
                   "numpy issues for similar problems.")
            raise RuntimeError(msg.format(__file__)) from None

    _sanity_check()
    del _sanity_check

    def _mac_os_check():
        """
        Quick Sanity check for Mac OS look for accelerate build bugs.
        Testing numpy polyfit calls init_dgelsd(LAPACK)
        """
        try:
            c = array([3., 2., 1.])
            x = linspace(0, 2, 5)
            y = polyval(c, x)
            _ = polyfit(x, y, 2, cov=True)
        except ValueError:
            pass

    if sys.platform == "darwin":
        from . import exceptions
        with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
            _mac_os_check()
            # Throw runtime error, if the test failed
            # Check for warning and report the error_message
            if len(w) > 0:
                for _wn in w:
                    if _wn.category is exceptions.RankWarning:
                        # Ignore other warnings, they may not be relevant (see gh-25433)
                        error_message = (
                            f"{_wn.category.__name__}: {_wn.message}"
                        )
                        msg = (
                            "Polyfit sanity test emitted a warning, most likely due "
                            "to using a buggy Accelerate backend."
                            "\nIf you compiled yourself, more information is available at:"  # noqa: E501
                            "\nhttps://numpy.org/devdocs/building/index.html"
                            "\nOtherwise report this to the vendor "
                            f"that provided NumPy.\n\n{error_message}\n")
                        raise RuntimeError(msg)
                del _wn
            del w
    del _mac_os_check

    def blas_fpe_check():
        if sys.platform != "darwin":
            # We currently assume this is limited to MacOS as downstream NumPy
            # import during dlopen caused a deadlock regression: gh-31284
            return

        # Check if BLAS adds spurious FPEs, seen on M4 arms with Accelerate.
        # In this case we disable FPE reporting since the use of SME poisons
        # it and Accelerate doesn't sanitize them.
        with errstate(all='raise'):
            x = ones((20, 20))
            try:
                x @ x
            except FloatingPointError:
                res = _core._multiarray_umath._blas_supports_fpe(False)
                if res:  # res was not modified (hardcoded to True for now)
                    warnings.warn(
                        "Spurious warnings given by blas but suppression not "
                        "set up on this platform. Please open a NumPy issue.",
                        UserWarning, stacklevel=2)

    blas_fpe_check()
    del blas_fpe_check

    def hugepage_setup():
        """
        We usually use madvise hugepages support, but on some old kernels it
        is slow and thus better avoided. Specifically kernel version 4.6
        had a bug fix which probably fixed this:
        https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/7cf91a98e607c2f935dbcc177d70011e95b8faff
        """
        use_hugepage = os.environ.get("NUMPY_MADVISE_HUGEPAGE", None)
        if sys.platform == "linux" and use_hugepage is None:
            # If there is an issue with parsing the kernel version,
            # set use_hugepage to 0. Usage of LooseVersion will handle
            # the kernel version parsing better, but avoided since it
            # will increase the import time.
            # See: #16679 for related discussion.
            try:
                use_hugepage = 1
                kernel_version = os.uname().release.split(".")[:2]
                kernel_version = tuple(int(v) for v in kernel_version)
                if kernel_version < (4, 6):
                    use_hugepage = 0
            except ValueError:
                use_hugepage = 0
        elif use_hugepage is None:
            # This is not Linux, so it should not matter, just enable anyway
            use_hugepage = 1
        else:
            use_hugepage = int(use_hugepage)
        return use_hugepage

    # Note that this will currently only make a difference on Linux
    _core.multiarray._set_madvise_hugepage(hugepage_setup())
    del hugepage_setup

    # Give a warning if NumPy is reloaded or imported on a sub-interpreter
    # We do this from python, since the C-module may not be reloaded and
    # it is tidier organized.
    _core.multiarray._multiarray_umath._reload_guard()

    # TODO: Remove the environment variable entirely now that it is "weak"
    if (os.environ.get("NPY_PROMOTION_STATE", "weak") != "weak"):
        warnings.warn(
            "NPY_PROMOTION_STATE was a temporary feature for NumPy 2.0 "
            "transition and is ignored after NumPy 2.2.",
            UserWarning, stacklevel=2)

    # Tell PyInstaller where to find hook-numpy.py
    def _pyinstaller_hooks_dir():
        from pathlib import Path
        return [str(Path(__file__).with_name("_pyinstaller").resolve())]


# Remove symbols imported for internal use
del os, sys, warnings

"""CPU-only exact FP16 eligibility screen; no framework/model initialization."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import math
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from argparse import ArgumentParser
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

import numpy as np

from benchmarks.analysis.evidence import freeze_sources
from wyat.backends.kai.artifact import load_artifact, positive_integer
from wyat.wire import decode_json

type Role = Literal["gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj"]
ROLES: tuple[Role, ...] = ("gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj")


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Arm:
    name: str
    layers: tuple[int, ...]
    roles: tuple[Role, ...]
    diagnostic_only: bool = False

    def names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return tuple(
            f"layers.{layer}.mlp.{role}.weight"
            for layer in self.layers
            for role in self.roles
        )


def declared_arms(layers: int) -> tuple[Arm, ...]:
    count = positive_integer(layers, "layers")
    all_layers = tuple(range(count))
    return (
        Arm("all-down", all_layers, ("down_proj",)),
        Arm("all-gate-up", all_layers, ("gate_proj", "up_proj")),
        Arm("all-mlp", all_layers, ROLES),
        Arm("first4-mlp", all_layers[:4], ROLES),
        Arm("last4-mlp", all_layers[-4:], ROLES),
        Arm("last1-mlp", all_layers[-1:], ROLES, diagnostic_only=True),
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class TensorSpan:
    name: str
    shape: tuple[int, int]
    offset: int
    elements: int


def projection_spans(
    path: Path, *, layers: int, hidden: int, intermediate: int
) -> tuple[TensorSpan, ...]:
    """Validate each selected BF16 tensor's exact shape and disjoint byte span."""
    for name, dimension in (
        ("layers", layers),
        ("hidden", hidden),
        ("intermediate", intermediate),
    ):
        positive_integer(dimension, name)
    size = path.stat().st_size
    with path.open("rb") as stream:
        raw_size = stream.read(8)
        if len(raw_size) != 8:
            raise ValueError("Truncated Safetensors length")
        header_size = struct.unpack("<Q", raw_size)[0]
        if not 0 < header_size <= min(8 << 20, size - 8):
            raise ValueError("Invalid Safetensors header length")
        header = decode_json(stream.read(header_size))
    if not isinstance(header, dict):
        raise ValueError("Safetensors header must be an object")
    origin = 8 + header_size
    spans: list[TensorSpan] = []
    for layer in range(layers):
        for role in ROLES:
            name = f"layers.{layer}.mlp.{role}.weight"
            entry = header.get(name)
            shape = (
                (hidden, intermediate)
                if role == "down_proj"
                else (intermediate, hidden)
            )
            if not isinstance(entry, dict) or entry.get("dtype") != "BF16":
                raise ValueError(f"Expected selected BF16 projection: {name}")
            actual_shape, offsets = entry.get("shape"), entry.get("data_offsets")
            if (
                not isinstance(actual_shape, list)
                or any(type(value) is not int for value in actual_shape)
                or actual_shape != list(shape)
                or not isinstance(offsets, list)
                or len(offsets) != 2
                or any(type(value) is not int for value in offsets)
            ):
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid selected projection shape/span: {name}")
            start, end = offsets
            # Narrowed JSON integer offsets are checked again for static typing.
            if type(start) is not int or type(end) is not int:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid offsets: {name}")
            elements = math.prod(shape)
            if start < 0 or end - start != elements * 2 or origin + end > size:
                raise ValueError(f"Selected projection span exceeds data: {name}")
            spans.append(TensorSpan(name, shape, origin + start, elements))
    ordered = sorted(spans, key=lambda item: item.offset)
    for left, right in zip(ordered, ordered[1:], strict=False):
        if left.offset + left.elements * 2 > right.offset:
            raise ValueError("Selected projection byte spans overlap")
    return tuple(spans)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class TensorEligibility:
    name: str
    shape: tuple[int, int]
    elements: int
    source_nonfinite: int
    mismatches: int
    overflow: int
    underflow_to_zero: int
    source_subnormal: int
    max_finite_absolute_error: float

    @property
    def eligible(self) -> bool:
        return self.source_nonfinite == 0 and self.mismatches == 0


def scan_tensor(
    path: Path, span: TensorSpan, *, chunk_elements: int = 1 << 18
) -> TensorEligibility:
    """Decode BF16 exactly, then compare FP16→FP32 values in bounded chunks.

    Overflow is reported separately: its absolute error is infinite, so the
    finite maximum alone is not an upper bound when overflow is nonzero.
    """
    positive_integer(chunk_elements, "chunk_elements")
    nonfinite = mismatches = overflow = underflow = subnormal = 0
    maximum = 0.0
    with path.open("rb") as stream:
        stream.seek(span.offset)
        for start in range(0, span.elements, chunk_elements):
            count = min(chunk_elements, span.elements - start)
            data = stream.read(count * 2)
            if len(data) != count * 2:
                raise ValueError(f"Truncated projection data: {span.name}")
            bits = np.frombuffer(data, dtype="<u2")
            original = (bits.astype(np.uint32) << 16).view(np.float32)
            with np.errstate(over="ignore", invalid="ignore", under="ignore"):
                restored = original.astype(np.float16).astype(np.float32)
            finite = np.isfinite(original)
            restored_finite = np.isfinite(restored)
            nonfinite += int(np.count_nonzero(~finite))
            mismatches += int(np.count_nonzero(original != restored))
            overflow += int(np.count_nonzero(finite & ~restored_finite))
            underflow += int(
                np.count_nonzero(finite & (original != 0) & (restored == 0))
            )
            subnormal += int(
                np.count_nonzero(((bits & 0x7F80) == 0) & ((bits & 0x7F) != 0))
            )
            comparable = finite & restored_finite
            if np.any(comparable):
                maximum = max(
                    maximum,
                    float(np.max(np.abs(original[comparable] - restored[comparable]))),
                )
    return TensorEligibility(
        span.name,
        span.shape,
        span.elements,
        nonfinite,
        mismatches,
        overflow,
        underflow,
        subnormal,
        maximum,
    )


def arm_results(
    arms: tuple[Arm, ...], tensors: tuple[TensorEligibility, ...]
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    by_name = {tensor.name: tensor for tensor in tensors}
    if len(by_name) != len(tensors):
        raise ValueError("Duplicate tensor eligibility result")
    results: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for arm in arms:
        selected = [by_name[name] for name in arm.names()]
        results.append(
            {
                **asdict(arm),
                "eligible": all(item.eligible for item in selected),
                "selected_elements": sum(item.elements for item in selected),
                "ineligible_tensors": [
                    item.name for item in selected if not item.eligible
                ],
            }
        )
    return results


def study(model: Path, output: Path) -> int:
    if output.exists():
        raise FileExistsError("Preserve existing eligibility receipt")
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
    frozen = freeze_sources(
        {
            "runner": Path(__file__),
            "artifact": root / "wyat/backends/kai/artifact.py",
            "wire": root / "wyat/wire.py",
            "numpy": Path(np.__file__),
            "tests": root / "tests/analysis/test_mlx_eligibility.py",
            "declaration": root / "docs/analysis/selective-precision.md",
        },
        output,
    )
    receipt: dict[str, object] = {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "complete": False,
        "any_eligible": False,
        "source_hashes": frozen.hashes(),
        "source_archive": frozen.archive(),
        "numpy_version": np.__version__,
        "policy": (
            "finite exact BF16→FP32→FP16→FP32; selected MLP tensors only; "
            "no framework/model initialized"
        ),
    }
    started = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        artifact = load_artifact(model, 512)
        path = artifact.root / "backbone/model.safetensors"
        dimensions = {
            name: positive_integer(artifact.config.get(name), name)
            for name in ("num_hidden_layers", "hidden_size", "intermediate_size")
        }
        arms = declared_arms(dimensions["num_hidden_layers"])
        with path.open("rb") as stream:
            checkpoint_hash = hashlib.file_digest(stream, "sha256").hexdigest()
        receipt.update(
            model_id=artifact.model_id,
            arms=[asdict(arm) for arm in arms],
            checkpoint_sha256=checkpoint_hash,
        )
        spans = projection_spans(
            path,
            layers=dimensions["num_hidden_layers"],
            hidden=dimensions["hidden_size"],
            intermediate=dimensions["intermediate_size"],
        )
        tensors: list[TensorEligibility] = []
        for span in spans:
            tensors.append(scan_tensor(path, span))
            receipt["tensors"] = [
                {**asdict(item), "eligible": item.eligible} for item in tensors
            ]
            output.write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n")
        results = arm_results(arms, tuple(tensors))
        with path.open("rb") as stream:
            final_hash = hashlib.file_digest(stream, "sha256").hexdigest()
        receipt["checkpoint_after_sha256"] = final_hash
        if final_hash != checkpoint_hash:
            raise ValueError("Checkpoint changed during parameter scan")
        receipt.update(
            arm_results=results,
            any_eligible=any(result["eligible"] is True for result in results),
            complete=True,
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        receipt.update(
            error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", complete=False, any_eligible=False
        )
    finally:
        receipt["elapsed_seconds"] = time.perf_counter() - started
        output.write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n")
    return 0 if receipt["complete"] and receipt["any_eligible"] else 1


def main() -> int:
    parser = ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--model", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--worker", action="store_true")
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    model, output = Path(arguments.model), Path(arguments.output)
    if arguments.worker:
        return study(model, output)
    return launch(model, output)


def launch(model: Path, output: Path) -> int:
    """Bound only our owned CPU scan and preserve timeout/error as non-passes."""
    wall = output.with_suffix(".wall.json")
    if output.exists() or wall.exists():
        raise FileExistsError("Preserve existing eligibility receipts")
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    command = [
        sys.executable,
        "-m",
        "benchmarks.analysis.mlx.eligibility",
        "--worker",
        "--model",
        str(model.resolve()),
        "--output",
        str(output.resolve()),
    ]
    receipt: dict[str, object] = {
        "command": command,
        "timeout_seconds": 120,
        "completed": False,
        "timed_out": False,
    }
    wall.write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2) + "\n")
    start = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(command, check=False, timeout=120)
        code = result.returncode
        receipt["completed"] = True
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        receipt["timed_out"] = True
        code = 124
    except OSError as exc:
        receipt["error"] = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
        code = 1
    receipt.update(exit_code=code, elapsed_seconds=time.perf_counter() - start)
    wall.write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n")
    return code


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
import struct
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from hypothesis import given
from hypothesis import strategies as st

from benchmarks.analysis.mlx.eligibility import (
    TensorEligibility,
    TensorSpan,
    arm_results,
    declared_arms,
    launch,
    projection_spans,
    scan_tensor,
    study,
)


def write_bits(path: Path, bits: list[int]) -> TensorSpan:
    path.write_bytes(struct.pack(f"<{len(bits)}H", *bits))
    return TensorSpan("probe", (1, len(bits)), 0, len(bits))


def test_exact_range_and_bf16_exponent_counterexamples(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    # ±1, signed zeros and the smallest half subnormal are exact. BF16 has
    # smaller subnormals and larger finite values that half cannot preserve.
    bits = [0x3F80, 0xBF80, 0, 0x8000, 0x3380, 0x0001, 0x7F7F]
    path = tmp_path / "bits"
    result = scan_tensor(path, write_bits(path, bits), chunk_elements=2)
    assert result.elements == 7
    assert result.source_nonfinite == 0
    assert result.mismatches == 2
    assert result.underflow_to_zero == 1
    assert result.source_subnormal == 1
    assert result.overflow == 1
    assert not result.eligible


def test_half_subnormal_grid_rounding_is_not_zero_underflow(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    path = tmp_path / "bits"
    # 2**-24 + 2**-31 is BF16-representable but not a half subnormal grid point.
    result = scan_tensor(path, write_bits(path, [0x3381]))
    assert result.mismatches == 1
    assert result.underflow_to_zero == result.overflow == 0
    assert result.max_finite_absolute_error == 2**-31


def test_nonfinite_source_fails_even_if_infinity_roundtrips(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    path = tmp_path / "bits"
    result = scan_tensor(path, write_bits(path, [0x7F80, 0xFF80, 0x7FC1]))
    assert result.source_nonfinite == 3
    assert result.overflow == 0
    assert not result.eligible


@given(st.lists(st.integers(0, 65535), min_size=1, max_size=64))
def test_chunked_scan_matches_independent_python_half_oracle(bits: list[int]) -> None:
    # NamedTemporaryFile avoids Hypothesis retaining a pytest tmp_path fixture.
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

    expected_mismatch = expected_nonfinite = 0
    for word in bits:
        value = struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<I", word << 16))[0]
        expected_nonfinite += not math.isfinite(value)
        try:
            restored = struct.unpack("<e", struct.pack("<e", value))[0]
        except OverflowError:
            restored = math.copysign(math.inf, value)
        expected_mismatch += value != restored
    with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
        path = Path(directory) / "bits"
        span = write_bits(path, bits)
        result = scan_tensor(path, span, chunk_elements=3)
        assert result.mismatches == expected_mismatch
        assert result.source_nonfinite == expected_nonfinite
        assert result.eligible == (expected_mismatch == expected_nonfinite == 0)


def fixture_file(path: Path, *, change: str = "") -> None:
    header: dict[str, object] = {}
    for index, role in enumerate(("gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj")):
        shape = [2, 1] if role != "down_proj" else [1, 2]
        header[f"layers.0.mlp.{role}.weight"] = {
            "dtype": "BF16",
            "shape": shape,
            "data_offsets": [4 * index, 4 * index + 4],
        }
    first = header["layers.0.mlp.gate_proj.weight"]
    assert isinstance(first, dict)
    if change == "dtype":
        first["dtype"] = "F16"
    elif change == "shape":
        first["shape"] = [True, 2]
    elif change == "outside":
        first["data_offsets"] = [100, 104]
    elif change == "overlap":
        first["data_offsets"] = [4, 8]
    elif change == "short":
        first["data_offsets"] = [0, 2]
    encoded = json.dumps(header).encode()
    path.write_bytes(struct.pack("<Q", len(encoded)) + encoded + bytes(12))


def test_only_declared_mlp_projections_and_shapes_are_selected(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    path = tmp_path / "fixture"
    fixture_file(path)
    spans = projection_spans(path, layers=1, hidden=1, intermediate=2)
    assert len(spans) == 3 and sum(item.elements for item in spans) == 6
    assert spans[-1].shape == (1, 2)
    assert all(scan_tensor(path, span).eligible for span in spans)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("change", ["dtype", "shape", "outside", "overlap", "short"])
def test_malformed_selected_projection_fails_closed(
    tmp_path: Path, change: str
) -> None:
    path = tmp_path / "fixture"
    fixture_file(path, change=change)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        projection_spans(path, layers=1, hidden=1, intermediate=2)


def test_truncated_stream_never_counts_as_exact(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    path = tmp_path / "bits"
    path.write_bytes(bytes(2))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Truncated"):
        scan_tensor(path, TensorSpan("probe", (1, 2), 0, 2))


def test_arm_eligibility_uses_exact_role_and_layer_intersections() -> None:
    arms = declared_arms(8)
    tensors = tuple(
        TensorEligibility(
            name,
            (1, 1),
            1,
            0,
            int(name == "layers.0.mlp.gate_proj.weight"),
            0,
            0,
            0,
            0.0,
        )
        for name in arms[2].names()
    )
    results = arm_results(arms, tensors)
    assert [item["eligible"] for item in results] == [
        True,
        False,
        False,
        False,
        True,
        True,
    ]
    assert results[-1]["diagnostic_only"] is True
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        arm_results(arms, tensors[:-1])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Duplicate"):
        arm_results(arms, (*tensors, tensors[0]))


def test_parent_timeout_preserves_partial_child_receipt(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    output = tmp_path / "result.json"

    def timeout(command: list[str], *, check: bool, timeout: int) -> None:
        output.write_text('{"complete": false}\n')
        raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(command, timeout)

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", timeout)
    assert launch(tmp_path / "model", output) == 124
    wall = json.loads(output.with_suffix(".wall.json").read_text())
    assert wall["timed_out"] is True and wall["completed"] is False
    assert json.loads(output.read_text())["complete"] is False
    with pytest.raises(FileExistsError):
        launch(tmp_path / "model", output)


def test_unexpected_artifact_failure_cannot_become_pass(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    output = tmp_path / "result.json"
    assert study(tmp_path / "absent-model", output) == 1
    result = json.loads(output.read_text())
    assert result["complete"] is False and result["any_eligible"] is False
    assert result["error"].startswith("FileNotFoundError")
